versions.title: 5 places to visit in Matsumoto: castle, old streets and a park
Qué ver en Matsumoto: 5 lugares entre el castillo y sus calles históricas
5 places to visit in Pátzcuaro’s historic centre
Qué ver en Pátzcuaro: 5 lugares del centro histórico
Things to do in Perugia: 5 places in the historic centre
Qué ver en Perugia: 5 lugares y una ruta por el centro histórico

notes: Six complete ES/EN manuscripts were read by the root Codex reviewer and independently checked by a Codex AI peer; all nine editorial checks were completed before approval. No human review or personal travel experience is claimed.

Twenty-four official documents were actually accessed and read with HTTP status, final URL, UTC capture time, byte SHA256, facts and locating excerpts. Historical material supports history and geography, not unverified current prices, programmes or timetables. Failed and unused source attempts remain recorded.

Matsumoto distinguishes the national-treasure castle from the separate Kaichi school museum and the later former Matsumoto High School buildings in Agata Forest Park. Castle stairs, entry points, visitor calendars and station bus facilities are described cautiously. No UNESCO status or universal transport-card coverage is invented.

Perugia distinguishes outdoor heritage stops from separately regulated palace rooms and museums. Sciri has232steps and limited accessibility; admission follows the operator calendar rather than a daily opening promise. The griffin and lion outside Palazzo dei Priori are copies; the originals are in the atrium. Minimetrò terminals and intermediate stops are distinguished.

Pátzcuaro distinguishes the two central squares, Casa de los Once Patios, Sagrario and Basilica. Clean INAH historical sources and the municipal map support the route; unrelated compromised-site text was excluded. National-monument status and a2025UNESCO nomination are not presented as a World Heritage inscription. Worship and workshop access are conditional; no present lake service or event schedule is invented.

Each of fifteen recommended places has its own relevant licensed documentary photograph. The specific file pages and applicable CreativeCommons deeds were read; source bytes,51optimizedWebPs, dimensions, hashes, attribution, modifications and bilingual ALT are preserved. Root and independent image reviewers viewed all fifteen photographs. Commons/Flickr supplied renditions are labelled accurately; no generated or paid images or upscaling.

The three intents and localized slugs are absent from188previous originals and376localized versions. Language, factual parity, originality and published internal-link targets were checked. All existing articles, dates, photos,3Ddesign, advertisements, Analytics consent, disabledpopunder, SEOsource and the two-originals/noonMiami default remain unchanged. This explicit manual batch contains three originals. Localpublished means selection for mandatorybuild, not public success.

checks.facts: Read all six full manuscripts independently. Checked 24 retained official, operator and scholarly sources: each HTTP 200 response has matching raw-body SHA256, final URL and date, and all 72 recorded excerpts match visible HTML or extracted PDF text. Visually checked the Pátzcuaro map: five place names and relative positions agree with the guide. Inconsistent Basilica numbering is acknowledged and unused. Historical material does not establish current visitor access.
checks.sourceRelevance: Read every place and practical section against its named evidence. Matsumoto uses municipal tourism and actual operators; Perugia uses Umbria Tourism, the municipality and actual tower/Minimetro operators; Pátzcuaro uses INAH body text, the clean scholarly PDF and municipal map. Discarded homepage/footer spam supplies no facts. Castle website photographs are not reused.
checks.imageRights: Independently read all 15 individual photo rights pages and four applicable CC deeds from archived HTTP 200 bodies, matching their hashes to evidence. Exact Flickr ImageObject records and Commons licensing boxes identify the selected licenses and creators. BY 2.0, BY 2.5, BY-SA 2.0 and BY-SA 4.0 permit commercial adaptation subject to the recorded credit, license link, changes and ShareAlike. Independently checked all 66 source and derivative files using Sharp dimensions and SHA256; no enlargement.
checks.imageRelevance: Viewed all 15 documentary images in three city contact sheets and compared them with headings, source descriptions and bilingual ALT. Kaichi and the two merchant streets are distinct. Agatanomori documents a park path, not the former school facade. Perugia images show the five named monuments/garden; the fountain source was already black and white. Pátzcuaro images show two distinct squares, Basilica, Once Patios courtyard and Sagrario exterior arcade. Archive photos do not establish present access.
checks.language: Read both complete language versions for every topic, including the seven final wording refinements. Titles, slugs, descriptions, headings and FAQ are localized; practical facts agree across languages. No untranslated draft passages, false personal experience, search-volume claims or indexing promises.
checks.originality: Compared with 376 baseline published localized files representing 188 originals: no destination/intent or slug collision and no exact duplicate paragraph of at least 40 words. The highest five-word-shingle Jaccard similarity is below 0.002. This is a local catalogue check, not a claim to have searched every online text. Historical facts are paraphrased into original, place-specific planning advice.
checks.usefulness: Each guide answers a first-visit query with five developed physical places, a distinct documentary photo per place, concrete observations, practical planning, a coherent walking route, five FAQ and relevant onward guides. The count agrees in both languages. Each version contains 1,814–2,009 useful words without invented experiences or unsupported rankings.
checks.timeSensitiveFacts: Checked potentially volatile claims against current operator material. No numeric prices, fixed daily opening hours, bus frequencies or guaranteed interior access are advertised. Matsumoto timed tickets, Kuromon entrance, closed red bridge, stairs and slippers are documented. Perugia tower stairs, booking and mobility conditions are documented; old event calendars are not reused. Pátzcuaro national designation does not become a UNESCO inscription, and historic PDFs do not become current timetables.
checks.internalLinks: All 18 localized related-guide references resolve to existing baseline published JSON files in the correct locale, with localized slugs. Read their geographical relevance; no invented day-trip duration is claimed. Public HTML navigation, canonical/hreflang, sitemap and live URLs remain release checks owned by the parent, not claims of this editorial review.
